Choose the bandwidth for an asynchronous longitudinal fit

Source: R/kee_async.R
kee_async_cv.Rd

Select the bandwidth for kee_async() and return the fit at it. The default, method = "variance", selects the bandwidth that minimises the estimated variance of an asynchrony-corrected fit (kee_async(correct = "pairs") by default). method = "sync" selects it for the same fit by K-fold cross-validation over subjects, and method = "plain" is ordinary cross-validation of the uncorrected fit.

Usage

kee_async_cv(
  data_y,
  data_x,
  formula,
  id,
  time,
  h_grid = NULL,
  n_h = 100L,
  K = 5L,
  repeats = 1L,
  one_sided = FALSE,
  link = c("identity", "log", "logistic"),
  intercept = TRUE,
  maxit = 50L,
  tol = 1e-08,
  seed = NULL,
  quiet = FALSE,
  method = c("variance", "sync", "plain"),
  correct = c("pairs", "gaussian")
)

# S3 method for class 'cv.kee_async'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

data_y

Data frame of response occasions: one row per time the response was recorded. First argument, so the function pipes.

data_x

Data frame of covariate occasions: one row per time the covariates were recorded. Its time grid need not overlap data_y's at all.

formula

A two-sided formula, y ~ x1 + x2. The left-hand side is looked up in data_y and the right-hand side in data_x, which is the one unusual thing about this interface and follows from the data being in two tables: there is no single frame holding both.

id

Subject identifier naming a column present in both tables. Give it unquoted (id = subject), as a string (id = "subject"), or embraced (id = {{ col }}) when calling from inside another function. Non-numeric identifiers are allowed.

time

Observation time, naming a column present in both tables. Accepts the same three forms as id.

h_grid

Optional numeric vector of candidate bandwidths. When NULL a grid is built from the data; see Details.

n_h

Number of candidates in the default grid.

K

Number of folds. Reduced to the number of subjects if larger. Cross-validation methods only.

repeats

Number of independent random K-fold splits; the held-out loss is averaged over them. Cross-validation methods only.

one_sided

Logical. FALSE (default) is the full two-sided kernel of the paper; TRUE is the half kernel, admitting only covariate observations strictly before the response.

link

One of "identity" (closed form), "log" or "logistic" (Newton-Raphson).

intercept

Logical, include an intercept.

maxit, tol

Newton-Raphson controls, ignored when link = "identity" and correct = "none".

seed

Optional integer seed for the subject-to-fold assignment. Pass it (or call set.seed() first) to make the selection reproducible. Cross-validation methods only.

quiet

Logical; suppress progress output.

method

"variance" (default): the bandwidth minimising the estimated variance of the asynchrony-corrected fit. "sync": synchronous-loss cross-validation of the corrected fit. "plain": kernel-weighted cross-validation of the uncorrected fit. See Details.

correct

The correction used with method = "variance" or "sync": "pairs" (default) or "gaussian"; see kee_async().

x

A cv.kee_async object.

...

Ignored.

Value

An object of class cv.kee_async:

h_cv

The selected bandwidth.

fit

The kee_async() fit on all subjects at h_cv, with the chosen correct unless method = "plain".

cv_results

Data frame of h and the criterion. For "variance", trSV, \(\mathrm{tr}\{\hat\Sigma_X \hat V(h)\}\). For the cross-validation methods, cvloss (the intercept for "sync", the weighted held-out loss for "plain") and nfold_used, the number of folds over all repeats that produced a usable loss.

h_grid, fold_id, repeats, method, correct, seed, call

Selection metadata; fold_id and repeats are NULL for "variance".

Minimum-variance bandwidth (method = "variance")

The corrected equation has mean zero at the true coefficients for every \(h\) (see kee_async()), so the bandwidth affects only the variance and the mean squared error of \(\hat\beta(h)\) is its variance. The corrected equation is solved on all subjects at every candidate, and the selected \(h\) minimises $$\mathrm{tr}\{\hat\Sigma_X \hat V(h)\},$$ with \(\hat V(h)\) the sandwich variance of \(\hat\beta(h)\) and \(\hat\Sigma_X\) the second moment of \(X\) at the response times: the covariate rows weighted by the estimated intensity ratio \(\lambda_T / \lambda_S\) for correct = "pairs", unweighted for correct = "gaussian". The criterion is \(n\) times the expected squared prediction error \(E[\{X(T)^\top(\hat\beta - \beta_0)\}^2]\), and it does not depend on the scale of the covariates.

\(\hat V(h)\) converges at every point of the finite grid, so when \(V\) has a unique minimiser \(h^*\) on the grid the selected bandwidth equals \(h^*\) with probability tending to one. The estimate at the selected bandwidth is then asymptotically normal with variance \(V(h^*)\), and the Wald interval has its nominal level asymptotically. No assumption on the distribution of the covariates is involved beyond those of the corrected equation.

The default grid is n_h log-spaced bandwidths up to the largest within-subject lag \(|T_{ij} - S_{ik}|\), starting at the smallest \(h\) at which at least \(\lceil n^{1/2} \rceil\) subjects have a pair inside the kernel (for correct = "pairs", both a response-covariate pair and a covariate pair). K, repeats and seed are not used.

Synchronous-loss cross-validation (method = "sync")

For each candidate \(h\) and fold, the corrected equation is fitted on the training subjects. Every within-subject pair \((T, S)\) of the held-out subjects gets the unweighted loss of \(Y(T)\) against the fitted mean at \(X(S)\): squared error (identity), Poisson deviance (log) or Bernoulli log loss (logistic). The losses are regressed on an intercept and the entries of the estimated variogram matrix \(\hat\Gamma(|T - S|)\), \(\Gamma(u) = E[\{x(t) - x(t-u)\}\{x(t) - x(t-u)\}^\top]\), of the covariates that vary within subjects. The intercept, the held-out loss at zero asynchrony, is retained. Each entry of \(\hat\Gamma\) comes from isotonic regressions of squared increments of \(x_j\) and \(x_j + x_k\) on the lag. For the identity link and a stationary covariate the intercept's expectation is \(\sigma^2 + \delta_h^\top \Sigma_X \delta_h\), with \(\delta_h\) the error of the training fit, because the asynchrony part of the loss is exactly linear in \(\Gamma(u)\). Intercepts are averaged over folds (and over repeats splits) and the minimiser is selected.

A candidate is retained only when every fold produces a fit whose intercept is at least the mean saturated loss of the held-out pairs (\(\min_\eta\) of the loss: 0 for squared error and log loss, \(y - y \log y\) for the Poisson loss). An intercept below it comes from a degenerate fold fit.

The default grid is n_h log-spaced bandwidths up to the largest within-subject lag \(|T_{ij} - S_{ik}|\), starting at the smallest \(h\) at which every training fold has at least \(\lceil n_{\mathrm{train}}^{1/2} \rceil\) subjects with a pair inside the kernel (for correct = "pairs", both a response-covariate pair and a covariate pair). Below that, a fold fit uses a handful of pairs and its error does not shrink with \(n\).

The guarantee is consistency: the selected \(h\) lies on a finite grid on which every corrected fit is consistent. The criterion's differences between candidates are of the same order as its noise, so the selected \(h\) does not converge. Because the same subjects choose \(h\) and fit \(\beta\), the estimate at the selected \(h\) can carry a selection bias of the order of its standard error, and the Wald interval has no coverage guarantee.

Plain cross-validation (method = "plain")

Each candidate is fitted without correction and scored on the held-out subjects by the kernel-weighted squared error of the fitted mean at that bandwidth, $$ \frac{\sum_{i \in \mathrm{test}} \sum_j \sum_k W_h(T_{ij} - S_{ik}) [Y_i(T_{ij}) - g\{X_i(S_{ik})^\top \hat\beta\}]^2} {\sum_{i \in \mathrm{test}} \sum_j \sum_k W_h(T_{ij} - S_{ik})}.$$ The default grid runs from the smallest to the largest within-subject lag (positive lags \(T_{ij} - S_{ik}\) only when one_sided = TRUE; exact zeros excluded). A candidate is dropped only when it fails on every fold. This criterion is minimised at a bandwidth much smaller than the MSE-optimal one, and the uncorrected fit keeps a bias of the order of its standard error there.

How the folds are formed

Folds are formed over subjects, never over rows. Rows within a subject come from one trajectory, so splitting by row would put a subject on both sides of the split and leak the answer into the held-out score.

Always look at cv_results. If the minimum sits at an endpoint of the grid a warning is issued.

See also

kee_async()

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- sim_async_data(n = 150, beta = c(0.5, 1.5))
cv <- d$y |>
  kee_async_cv(d$x, y ~ x,
    id = id, time = time,
    n_h = 20, K = 3, seed = 1, quiet = TRUE
  )
#> Warning: the selected bandwidth is at an endpoint of 'h_grid'; widen the grid to check that the minimum is interior
